subject.title: feat: bind signed ClawHub default feed trust

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make all existing signed marketplace profiles invalid until operators add `feedId`, or should the trust-binding rollout include a supported Doctor-led migration or staged compatibility plan?
rationale: An arbitrary existing signed profile’s expected payload identity cannot safely be inferred from its URL, while silently preserving the prior unbound trust model would weaken the security goal; this is an upgrade-policy choice, not a mechanical reviewer decision.

options.title: Require a migration before merge
options.body: Add a Doctor-detected migration or explicit upgrade workflow that preserves valid existing deployments while requiring operators to confirm any non-inferable feed identity.

options.title: Accept the breaking config change
options.body: Land the mandatory `feedId` validation as a deliberate breaking upgrade, with release-owned communication and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Delay default activation
options.body: Keep the generic trust primitives but defer the default ClawHub signed-profile activation until the production key and rotation path are ready.

recommendation.title: Require a migration before merge
recommendation.body: Add a Doctor-detected migration or explicit upgrade workflow that preserves valid existing deployments while requiring operators to confirm any non-inferable feed identity.

likelyOwner.reason: The review discussion identifies Patrick-Erichsen as the person who requested the recent trust and expiry changes.
